new_statements.relation_note: Language has no catalog record and no statement held by the project; this copy adds none. (The handwritten original, not obtained, might carry accent marks: Reid 1994 cites no stress-marked AGTCS2 forms, only AGTCS4 = San Ramon ones.)
new_statements.rule_in_words: A bare 372-item survey wordlist in plain typescript: forms are given without any stress or accent marks (only the glottal stop is written, as a raised ˀ); there is no prose, no transcription note and no statement about stress anywhere in the file. Nothing about word-stress placement can be taken from this version.
new_statements.identity_note: Work 0 = Inagta of Sta Niño / Hayagan / Sta Cruz (Ipil), Buhi, Camarines Sur, elicited in Buhi from Mrs. Gabrillo, 16 Aug 1979 (Reid 1994's AGTCS2). Work 1's Agta column = 'San Ramon Agta', San Ramon, Lake Buhi, Camarines Sur (Reid 1994's AGTCS4); the SIL record files both under Mt. Iriga Agta [agz]. The other three columns of work 1 are Naga (Central) Bikol, Iriga (Rinconada) Bikol and Buhi'non Bikol, not Agta.

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record for mtir1235. First primary evidence held by the project of stress position in Mt. Iriga Agta words: 372 stress-marked San Ramon Agta forms showing both penultimate and final stress. Data only; no rule stated, so it supports 'lexical/contrastive penult-vs-final stress' only as an inference to be confirmed by a description (Villegas 2010 BA thesis; Fleischman & Nickell 1979 survey report, both unobtained).
new_statements.translation_language: English glosses; Bikol and San Ramon Agta
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule is STATED anywhere (data set only, no prose). What the data show: every San Ramon Agta form is transcribed with a stress mark placed before the stressed syllable, and the marked syllable is sometimes the penult (ʹsimbag 'answer', ʹbunga 'areca nut', ʹmanok 'chicken', ʹsukray 'comb', ʹdaghan 'chest', ʹbangkaʔ 'boat', ʹtila 'cotton') and sometimes the final syllable (abaʹka 'abaca', haʹpon 'afternoon', loʹbud 'anus', baʹtag 'banana', dakoʹlo 'big', buʹta 'blind', uʹwak 'crow', kaʹgat 'bite'); a crude count over the scanned text of the Agta column gives roughly 110 non-final vs 98 final marks. In my reading this is per-word (lexically specified) penult-or-final stress of the usual Central Philippine type, often differing from the Bikol cognate in the same row (Naga ʹbuta vs Agta buʹta 'blind'; Naga maʹnok vs Agta ʹmanok 'chicken'). this compilation is an inference from the transcribed forms, not a statement of the source.
new_statements.secondary_stress: not marked (one stress mark per word; a few reduplicated/compound forms carry none or two, e.g. buʹkubuʹku in the Naga column)

sources.citation: University of the Philippines Diliman, Department of Linguistics, The Katig Collective. 2024. Language capsule: Agta, Mt. Iriga.
sources.note: No phonology or stress information; notes only that the lexicon has loans from southern Bikol languages such as Rinconada Bikol; cites Ethnologue, Glottolog, Lobel 2013, Nickell 1979 and SIL 1984 wordlists.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. Section 3.2.3 'The Agta of Camarines Sur, Bikol: Rinconada Agta, Partido Agta, and East Lake Buhi Agta', pp. 68-72.
sources.note: Nothing for Inagta Rinconada: sec. 3.2.3 gives location, sociolinguistic status, lexical affinities (lexicon resembles Rinconada Bikol) and pronoun/case-marker/demonstrative tables whose forms carry acute accents (e.g. dodoón) but no phonology or stress statement. The only stress passages in the dissertation concern Manide/Inagta Alabat (sec. 8.2.9 'Contrastive accent', p. 259) and Maranao (fn. 3, p. 287: loss of contrastive stress in some Bikol-subgroup members, citing Lobel 2003 on Rinconada Bikol).

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2010. Manide: an undescribed Philippine language. Oceanic Linguistics 49(2): 478-510.
sources.note: Phonology is of Manide only. On the target it says (sec. 1) that Inagta Rinconada, Inagta Partido, Inagta Alabat and Manide have 'none.. received any substantial attention in the linguistics literature', and that the Rinconada/Partido Agta language 'is a member of the Bikol subgroup with very few features indicating any pre-Bikol substrata'. Cites Fleischman & Nickell 1979 SIL survey report. Nothing on Inagta Rinconada stress.

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 1994. Possible non-Austronesian lexical elements in Philippine Negrito languages. Oceanic Linguistics 33(1): 37-72 (ScholarSpace preprint pagination).
sources.note: Sec. 2.2.5 'South Agta' (p. 8): Camarines Sur Agta known only from several SIL wordlists taken near Lake Buhi, 'No morphological or syntactic data is available for these languages.' P. 10 transcription note: 'Where stress has been indicated, it is marked as an acute accent on the stressed vowel.' Appendix A (p. 30) lists four SIL Camarines Sur Agta lists (Rugnot, Lake Buhi; Inagta Sta Niño/Sta Cruz; Inagta San Augustine; Inagta San Ramon). Data items show acute on varying syllables (adíŋ 'fire', áŋas 'forehead', sogbóŋ ~ sógboŋ 'shoulder'); no rule stated.
